prompt: What does an integration/API test of a Flask endpoint (via app.test_client()) exercise that a Tier-1-style unit test of the same logic does not?
choices: Routing, request parsing, and response serialization together with the business logic, not just the logic in isolation
Nothing extra — they test exactly the same code paths
Only the database layer, never the view function
It replaces the need for any assertions on the response body

prompt: A module client.py does `from external_api import fetch_data` and calls `fetch_data()` directly inside a function. Which patch target correctly mocks that call in a test?
choices: patch("external_api.fetch_data")
patch("client.fetch_data")
patch("client.external_api.fetch_data")
Either of the first two works identically

prompt: Why does the test database fixture call create_all() and drop_all() around every single test function, rather than once for the whole test file?
choices: pytest requires create_all() to be called inside every test function or it raises an error
So each test starts from a known, empty database state and can't be affected by rows another test left behind
SQLite does not support running more than one test per file
It has no real effect on correctness, only on how long the suite takes to run

prompt: In the checkout_book endpoint, what status code should be returned when a client tries to check out a book that is already checked out (available is already False)?
choices: 200 OK
404 Not Found
409 Conflict
500 Internal Server Error

prompt: A test suite passes when each test file is run alone, but fails intermittently when the full suite runs together in one process. What does this most strongly suggest?
choices: The CI server has a hardware problem
Tests are not properly isolated — state from one test (e.g. a leftover database row) is leaking into another
Too many assertions were written in a single test function
The wrong HTTP verb was used on one of the routes

prompt: Why mock the third-party ISBN lookup service in the create_book tests instead of letting the test hit the real service over the network?
choices: Because Flask's test client physically blocks all outbound network calls
So tests stay fast, deterministic, and unaffected by the third party being slow, down, or rate-limiting you
Because the requests library cannot be used inside test files
To avoid needing an internet connection to write any Python code at all

prompt: Which library is the closest Node.js/Express equivalent to using Flask's app.test_client() for full HTTP-level endpoint testing?
choices: axios
supertest
lodash
nodemon

prompt: A team's integration tests run against an in-memory SQLite database and all pass, but the same feature breaks against the production Postgres database. What's the most likely explanation?
choices: SQLite runs queries too slowly to catch real bugs
SQLite enforces column types and constraints more loosely than Postgres, letting a bug through that Postgres would reject
pytest cannot generate valid SQL for Postgres
Postgres does not support returning JSON from an API
